one_line_summary: An oversized, ribbed, V-neck wool-blend cardigan with deep armholes and a generous body — the cardigan that launched a thousand IG saves and twice as many dupes.
energy: off-duty model — the cardigan that looks like you stole it from someone whose style you envy
pull_quote: Buy if you wear oversized as a default and your bottoms run slim. Pass if you're petite and dislike volume — this will swallow you, even in the smallest size.

verdicts.label: soft / generous / undone
verdicts.reasoning: This is the cardigan you keep saving on Pinterest. It does the over-the-shoulder thing, the buttoned-as-a-top thing, the layered-over-a-tee-and-jeans thing — all without looking like you tried. The wool blend has weight, so it drapes properly instead of sitting awkwardly. Worth the $185.

verdicts.label: delicate / fitted / scaled
verdicts.reasoning: Even the smallest size runs intentionally large. The deep armholes and dropped shoulders are designed for visual volume — on a smaller frame they read as 'borrowed from dad' rather than 'considered.' Look at Sézane Gaspard or Reformation Maddie cardigan instead — both come in true-to-size proportions.

verdicts.label: clean / sharp / restrained
verdicts.reasoning: It can work as a layering piece over a button-down with tailored trousers, but only in the navy or chocolate colorways — the cream version is too undone for your register. If you want oversized knit but with more structure, the Khaite Scarlet is the move.

verdicts.label: smart-shopper / dupe-aware
verdicts.reasoning: There are 15+ near-identical cardigans at $40-80 across H&M, Mango, Cos, and Quince that get you 80% of the look. The Bea's quality is real but not 3x-the-price real. Buy the dupe, save the difference for a piece where the quality gap actually shows (knit dresses, wool coats).

why_people_love_it: The drape is the whole point — most knockoffs look right on the hanger but go limp when worn. The Bea's wool content keeps it sculptural
The neutrals (oat, chocolate, navy) are genuinely versatile — 3 of these in different colors can build a whole capsule
Buttons are sturdy enough to wear it as a top with nothing underneath, which doubles its outfits
where_it_falls_flat: Pills under the arms within the first season — that's wool blend physics, not a defect, but expect maintenance
Restocks are unpredictable; if your size is in stock, it won't be next week
The white/cream colorway shows everything; if you're a coffee-spiller, get the chocolate

alternatives.name: Sézane Gaspard Cardigan
alternatives.reasoning: True-to-size cut with a similar V-neck and button placket. Slightly more polished, less Pinterest-girl. Better on shorter torsos.

alternatives.name: Quince Mongolian Cashmere V-Neck Cardigan
alternatives.reasoning: Actual cashmere at half the price. Slightly less oversized cut, but the fiber upgrade matters more than the silhouette difference. Real dupe that's arguably better quality.

alternatives.name: Khaite Scarlet Cardigan
alternatives.reasoning: Investment piece, very different price tier, but a fundamentally more refined garment — heavier knit, better shoulder construction, ages into a forever piece. Only worth it if knitwear is your category.
